## TL;DR

This pass found that task body updates made through `repoos update` bypassed the shared needs-input assessment that the UI PATCH route already ran. The CLI could therefore leave an incomplete task unflagged or preserve a stale spec-owned flag after the body was repaired. I aligned the CLI update path with the server, made its output report the resulting needs-input detail, and surfaced creation-time needs-input state in the task drawer. The focused regression test and the required scoped RepoOS check passed.

## Work and rationale

I started by tracing the task lifecycle at the boundaries users actually use: `repoos new`, `repoos update`, `POST /api/tasks`, and `PATCH /api/tasks/:id`. Task creation was already largely consistent. Both CLI and server creation run `flagTaskSpecFlagsIfNeededAsync`, which combines the underspecified-body assessment and human-step assessment. The CLI reports the resulting detail. The UI receives the created task, but the task drawer previously closed without surfacing that the server had marked the task as needing input. I added an informational toast using the returned reason/detail, with a fallback for cases where the server has no detail.

The important parity gap was in updates. The server PATCH handler reassesses after body, section, or assignee changes. The CLI update command applies its parsed patch directly through `patchTaskFile` and did not call that shared assessment. Since the assessment owns its own `underspecified` reason, calling it again also handles the repair case: it removes that flag when the body now passes, while preserving unrelated needs-input reasons and human questions. I added the same post-patch call to `cmdUpdate`, restricted to the same field changes as the route. When the resulting task still needs input, CLI output now includes its stored detail or reason so the wait state is visible without reopening the file.

I added a regression in the existing CLI board-write test suite. It first patches a task with a short but structurally preserved body and checks that `needs_input` and `underspecified` are written. It then replaces that body with a complete spec and checks that the assessment-owned flag is removed. This captures both the raise and clear paths, which are where divergence had practical impact.

I also wrote the QA findings and verification record to `docs/qa/2026-11-task-validation.md`. It explains the intentional behavior: incomplete agent tasks are saved and marked as needing input rather than rejected, so the owner can continue editing them. Human-assigned work is exempt from the agent body contract.

## Approaches tried

I first looked for a separate validation implementation to unify. That was not necessary: the shared core assessment already exists, and the server update path uses it. The narrow fix was to make the CLI call the same asynchronous function at the same update boundary, rather than duplicating or weakening the rules.

I ran the targeted test file first. It passed, including the new regression and the suite's isolated boot-timing pass. The required changed-path check initially stopped at formatting, before build and test steps. I ran `bun run fmt`, then reran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. The remote gate passed the changed-path suite, and local build, format/lint, CSS and theme guards, contrast audit, and headless UI smoke test all passed. I also started `just serve-noauth` from this task worktree and drove the dashboard, New task drawer, and an existing needs-input task drawer with headless Playwright. The form and task detail rendered without page errors; the existing needs-input task showed its next steps.

## Challenges and blockers

Port 7272 was already occupied, so I used 7273 and stopped the server after verification. The `serve-noauth` recipe runs in preview mode and is read-only. I did not submit a task from the browser, because that would either be rejected by the preview write guard or require writing QA data into this task branch. The new post-create toast is therefore verified through the build and source path, while end-to-end creation remains covered by the shared route behavior and focused unit/regression tests rather than an interactive mutation.

RepoOS wrote WIP checkpoint commits while running the scoped check. I did not stage or commit files manually. The latest check ran on the formatted tree; its remote gate and local steps passed.

## Key learnings

Task creation and task update have different server boundaries: creation reassessment happens in the create route or CLI constructor path, while update reassessment is a post-patch responsibility. Keeping the assessment centralized is not enough unless every mutation entry point invokes it.

The `needs_input_reason` and detail are durable workflow state, not merely warnings. A caller that changes the task body should recalculate the assessment-owned reason, but should not overwrite an unrelated human block. Reusing `flagTaskSpecFlagsIfNeededAsync` preserves that ownership behavior and keeps UI and CLI semantics aligned.

A needs-input task should remain available for repair, and the interface should say why it is waiting. The UI toast now communicates the creation result, and the CLI communicates the same stored detail after an update.
